title: Finite and integral exceptional operation families
statement: For the fixed prime, algebraic closure, finite-field datum, morphism and compactification, there exist operation and compact-support left-realization families for every finite and integral RingStage.

source.place: Constructions 4.1 and 5.25, Lemma 5.22 and Propositions 5.24 and 5.26

proof.text: At a positive finite stage write its exponent as m+1. Obtain a finite dimension bound for c.Z using its finite-type structure map c.g followed by the map Y to Spec(D.k). Apply exists_sfFiniteExceptionalOperations, retain the actual F,G, their additive and shift structures, their adjunction, exactness and shift-compatible unit and counit, and package them as Operation. Compose eqToIso of the literal left inclusion equality with the inverse finiteImageIso to obtain LeftRealization.

At an integral stage apply exists_integral_support_adjoint to obtain preservation and the IsLeftAdjoint instance for the literal full-subcategory lift of ambient compact support. Define F to be precisely that lift and G its right adjoint. The liftCompιIso is the required LeftRealization, without any further choice of ambient functor.

Use the inherited triangulation of the integral finite-Tor predicates and the fully faithful ambient inclusion. Compose the inclusion shift with the actual compact-support shift. Functor.CommShift.ofComp lifts it to F, and isTriangulated_iff_comp_right reflects exactness from the compact-support composite. Equip G with adj.rightAdjointCommShift. The adjunction supplies right additivity, shift compatibility of its unit and counit, and exactness of G. This fills every field of Operation.

For each RingStage use the corresponding finite or integral existence proof, then choose its operation and realization witnesses to obtain the two dependent families. Return these with True.intro. No scalar comparison or extra geometric hypothesis is required. The existing preservation and finite operation declarations apply also to empty schemes, and the positive finite decomposition includes exponent one.

proof_origin.place: Constructions 4.1 and 5.25, Lemma 5.22 and Propositions 5.24 and 5.26; reuse the existing finite operations and integral restricted support adjoint, then assemble by RingStage (B9)

lean.statement:
theorem exists_exceptional_ring_operations
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω]
    [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω] (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (c : Compactification f) :
    ∃ operation : ∀ s : RingStage.{u} l, Operation.{u} l Ω X Y (s.stage l),
      ∃ left : ∀ s : RingStage.{u} l,
        LeftRealization.{u} l Ω c s (operation s), True
